clue.text: Stop! The holiday's cancelled

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday; the 's stands for 'is'
an event called off is said to be off

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in dismay on learning their trip has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease doing something is a common idiomatic meaning of the phrasal verb, often shouted as a command.

clue.text: He makes a crust with very little effort

definitions.text: He makes a crust with very little effort

parts.words: He makes a crust with very little effort
parts.note: earning a crust is making a living; an idler does it lazily, and a loaf of bread has a crust

explanation.surface: A baker turns out bread effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a crust' is British slang for earning a living; a loaf has a crust.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler does as little work as possible, barely earning a living.

clue.text: More Liberal politician in real trouble!

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
letters in trouble are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is in genuine difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks political but means generous; 'trouble' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal here means generous or plentiful, so more liberal is more abundant.

clue.text: Freed from liability, Devon banker and Frenchman take little part

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a county in south-west England; a river has banks
M is short for monsieur
pt is the abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: A Devon bank official and a Frenchman escape liability by playing a minor role.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Released from an obligation means not subject to it.

clue.text: Just a horse-but that's quite a lot

parts.note: just means fair, impartial
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: Only a horse, yet that is a considerable sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasonable quantity, a sizeable sum, is quite a lot.

clue.text: Puts one's foot down and makes an impression

explanation.surface: A forceful person asserts themselves and gets noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is bringing a foot down hard; the other is printing a mark, as a rubber seal does on paper.

clue.text: Will she raise the roof in the House?

definitions.text: Will she raise the roof in the House?

parts.words: Will she raise the roof in the House?
parts.note: a straw-roofing craftsman puts up roofs; the famous prime minister of that name made a noise in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Asks whether a female MP will cause uproar in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was the British prime minister 1979-90; a thatcher builds straw roofs.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who roofs with straw literally raises a roof, and the PM caused uproar in Parliament.

clue.text: Wrongly report the winner of an art gallery beauty contest?

definitions.text: Wrongly report the winner of an art gallery beauty contest?

parts.words: Wrongly report the winner of an art gallery beauty contest?
parts.note: a beauty queen is titled Miss plus a place; the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone misreports who won a beauty pageant held at a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous London art gallery; a beauty winner from there would be Miss Tate.
explanation.definitionFit: To misreport or give incorrect facts is a verb meaning to report wrongly.

clue.text: Nice organisation in safe surroundings makes for an easy job

indicators.note: the safe word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: sure means safe, certain

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A tidy setup in secure premises makes for a comfortable post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city or an adjective; 'organisation' is the anagram signal and 'surroundings' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A post with pay but few duties is a cushy job.

clue.text: Such a bed can't possibly be sweet

definitions.text: Such a bed can't possibly be sweet

parts.words: Such a bed can't possibly be sweet
parts.note: a prank bed with the sheet folded so the sleeper cannot stretch out shares its name with a dessert, yet it is no pudding

explanation.surface: A bed so uncomfortable that it could never be pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: An apple-pie bed is a British schoolboy prank: the sheet is folded back so the legs cannot go down. The clue plays on the dessert of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The prank bed carries the name of a sweet baked pudding, which the clue says it cannot be.

clue.text: Minister would put equal value on a child

parts.note: par means equality of value, as in 'on a par'
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A clergyman insists on valuing a child as an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish clergyman ministers to a congregation, so he is a minister of religion.

clue.text: The ideal perm Alex devised

indicators.note: something devised is put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alex has invented the perfect hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges PERM and ALEX together; 'perm' looks like a hairdo but is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A model or perfect pattern to be copied is the ideal.

clue.text: Sour airman with a nervous spasm

parts.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A grumpy pilot suffers from a nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar-like, from acetic acid, means tasting sour.

clue.text: Used another workman

parts.note: a second is another one
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: An employer took on a further labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods previously owned by someone else are used.

clue.text: It's endearing terms mean nothing to a landlord

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
one who lets property is a letter

explanation.surface: Affectionate words are meaningless to a property owner.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter is literally 'one who lets', so a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic note to a sweetheart is written in endearing terms.

clue.text: Ready-cut, and ready for use

explanation.surface: Food that is pre-cut and ready to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits as PRE-PARED: trimmed in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is pared beforehand; the other is made ready.

clue.text: When it comes to theological commitment, he is coasting freely

definitions.text: When it comes to theological commitment, he

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: In matters of faith, he simply drifts along without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coasting freely' reads as idle drifting, but 'freely' rearranges COASTING.
explanation.definitionFit: One who holds that God's existence is unknowable makes no religious commitment.

clue.text: Walked slowly along the street and staggered from side to side

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
rolled means swayed, as a ship or drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk ambled down the road, lurching about.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble at a leisurely pace is to walk slowly.

clue.text: The Tories are heading the polls and riding high

definitions.text: The Tories are heading the polls

explanation.surface: Election news: the Conservatives lead and are doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are the political right, so 'the right on top' describes them leading the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings mean being in the lead: the right wing winning, and anyone enjoying success.

clue.text: Call off the act and ring the changes again

explanation.surface: Parliament cancels a law and makes fresh adjustments.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as RE-PEAL: bells peal again, and change-ringing is a style of bell-ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is revoking a law; the other is sounding bells once more.

clue.text: The very last point won by Wimbledon champions

parts.note: final means last of all
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Champions at the tennis championship take the deciding point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, not a tennis point. Wimbledon is the London tennis championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Champions must win the deciding matches of a tournament, the plural noun for them.

clue.text: Execute advice given to an ambitious teacher

definitions.text: advice given to an ambitious teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher is urged to put someone to death, or to seek promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as 'Be head': aim to become head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is decapitating someone; the other urges a teacher to become principal.

clue.text: Professional has great weight in a nuclear centre

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: An expert carries heavy responsibility at an atomic research site.
explanation.definitionFit: This particle sits in the nucleus of an atom, at its very core.

clue.text: He's caught in a low-class den, by gum

indicators.note: something caught in a place is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man is arrested in a seedy club, and the speaker exclaims 'by gum!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by gum' looks like a mild oath, but 'by' is a link and 'gum' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum is a sticky substance, a glue, used to make things stick.

clue.text: Noisy toy may cause exasperation

explanation.surface: A baby's toy can drive parents mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's shaken plaything makes noise; as a verb it means to unsettle or annoy someone.

clue.text: Brave opponent, but he doesn't look it

definitions.text: Brave opponent, but he doesn't look it

parts.words: Brave opponent, but he doesn't look it
parts.note: a Native American warrior is a brave; his white enemy in Westerns has a pallid face, the look of someone afraid

explanation.surface: A courageous adversary who looks timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is the noun for a Native American warrior, not the adjective; a pale face suggests fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Westerns use this name for a white settler, enemy of the warrior, whose complexion suggests cowardice.

clue.text: What cryptanalysts do to a Christmas poem?

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated Dec
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Code-breakers puzzle over a festive verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Code-breakers translate ciphers into plain text, their job description.

clue.text: Did I lose out on being worshipped?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they missed out on being adored.
explanation.definitionFit: To be adored like a god or star is to be worshipped.
